claims.statement: The ci.yml workflow runs on pushes to main, pull requests, and manual dispatch; cancels superseded runs per workflow and ref; calls reusable test, lint, and documentation workflows; and performs read-only merge-marker, cross-reference, external-documentation-URL, and generated-file checks.

The reusable test and lint workflows accept caller-supplied Python and working-directory inputs, install the test dependency group with uv, and run make test or make lint; the test workflow additionally runs make test_integration for ./libs/server, while the documentation workflow has contents: read, a 20-minute timeout, Mintlify CLI version 4.2.1181, and runs anchor-link, MDX, and OpenAPI checks.

The repository's documentation-specific pull-request checks lint only changed src Markdown or MDX files with the pinned Vale installation and reject links to retired documentation sites, using read-only contents permissions.

The preview workflow gives contents write only to preview creation and cleanup, pull-requests write only to the comment job, skips write-capable preview creation for fork pull requests, builds documentation, and creates a deterministic preview-<slug>-<sha256-prefix> branch that is updated with force-with-lease.
On pull-request close, preview cleanup recomputes the deterministic branch and legacy preview names, deletes only matching branches, and refuses deletion unless a candidate begins with preview-.

After a successful preview branch build, the comment job requires MINTLIFY_API_KEY and MINTLIFY_PROJECT_ID, calls the Mintlify preview API, and replaces prior bot preview comments with a preview link and at most five changed routable documentation deep links while excluding code samples and snippets.

The publish workflow runs on pushes to main or manual dispatch, builds documentation with Python 3.13, verifies build/, copies it under public/build, and uses peaceiris/actions-gh-pages with GITHUB_TOKEN and contents write permission to publish the result to the prod branch.

Integration submission automation starts only from manual dispatch or an issue labeled integration-run, uses a per-issue non-canceling concurrency group, grants contents, pull-request, and issue write permissions, and authorizes the triggering actor by requiring admin, maintain, or write collaborator permission before processing the issue.

The integration submission workflow parses structured issue fields before invoking Deep Agents, treats parsed values as untrusted metadata, marks automation in progress, and handles parse errors, hard-blocker files, agent failures, no-change results, and successful edits as distinct outcomes.

When integration automation produces real edits, it mints the GitHub App token only after the agent step, then creates or updates a review PR on integration/issue-<number>, labels and assigns it, and comments the PR link on the source issue without merging it.

The external integration PR workflow uses pull_request_target with contents read, issues read, and pull-requests write permissions, inspects changed files and fork-head content through GitHub APIs without executing untrusted code, labels qualifying external contributions, and redirects and closes non-featured additions below 50,000 monthly downloads while honoring maintainer reopen overrides.

CODEOWNERS assigns @lnhsingh as the default owner for repository tooling and unowned files, assigns integration listings to @npentrel, and relies on GitHub's last-matching-rule behavior for more specific product ownership.

The pull-request template requires contributors to explain the change, provide review notes and related references, and check documentation policy, preview, examples, prose lint, link validation, and navigation requirements.
